answer: A sybil farmer's edge is zero marginal cost: shell 1 and shell 1,000 cost the same to mint. Break that symmetry with superlinear marginal identity pricing. Linkage signals — shared funding sources, invite trees, correlated behavior — cluster identities by probable operator, and the nth identity in a cluster costs n-squared copper to register, recorded on the onyx ledger. Rewards grow linearly, so past the knee each new shell loses money; expansion ripples the operator's own cost curve upward. Imperfect detection degrades gracefully: a false positive pays a slightly higher fee, never a ban.
